_readme: Dual Threat clue sets. One entry per athlete, linked by ModiDex athlete id. 'pokemon' must match that athlete's ModiDex comp (a guard: if ModiDex changes the comp, the set is skipped until you update it). 4-5 clues, vague to specific, each describing BOTH. Tokens filled from live ModiDex data: {sport} {team} {position} {number} {division}. Add a new set with: node tools/new-clue.mjs <athlete name>. Check with: node tools/validate.mjs

clues: It makes the hardest parts of its job look almost too easy.
It's at its most dangerous when everything around it breaks down.
Its mind races faster than anyone's, and it can deliver from any angle without even looking.
Psychic-level brilliance from the {position} spot, with multiple {sport} MVPs and Super Bowl rings.
Wears #{number} for the {team} and solves defenses while gripping a spoon in each hand.
sets.why: Mahomes and Alakazam are both genius minds: Alakazam's IQ is said to be 5,000, and Mahomes sees throws (and no-look angles) nobody else does.

clues: It's built bigger and tougher than most others in its line of work.
Once it starts running, it doesn't stop until something gets knocked over.
Raised on a farm, it grew into a huge, rugged beast that loves contact.
A no-evolution Normal-type... and a cannon-armed {position} who has hurdled defenders in the {sport}.
Plays for the {team} in the snow, and it's a charging bull that whips itself with its three tails.
sets.why: Josh Allen plays like Tauros charges: head down, full speed, through whoever is in front of him. A bull for Buffalo just fits.

clues: Opponents who reach for it usually grab nothing but air.
It strikes so suddenly that it's gone before anyone can react.
It crackles with electricity every time it takes off, and many already call it a legend.
An Electric legend... and a Heisman-winning {position} who went 32nd overall and won {sport} MVP twice.
Wears #{number} for the {team}, and it's the yellow, spiky thunderbird of Kanto's legendary trio.
sets.why: Lamar Jackson is lightning in cleats, a legendary talent no defender can catch, just like the thunderbird Zapdos. A legendary bird for the Ravens.

clues: It carries itself with a quiet confidence that rivals find unsettling.
It picks apart opponents with surgical precision, one clean cut at a time.
Its frosty calm became legendary during one unbeaten championship season.
An Ice-type legendary bird... and a Heisman-winning {position} who went first overall in the {sport} draft.
Wears #{number} for the {team}, celebrated a title with a cigar, and it's the icy blue legendary bird.
sets.why: Joe Burrow is the coolest customer in football, calm under any pressure, so his match is Articuno, the legendary bird of ice.

clues: It does its job the same way every day, no matter what anyone says.
It's built low, thick and sturdy, and its expression rarely changes.
Its best weapon is a short, straight-ahead shove that bulldozes everything in front of it.
A Ground/Rock beast in its first form... and a {position} who began at Alabama before transferring.
Wears #{number} for the {team}, made the tush push famous, and it's a gray, spiky charging rhino.
sets.why: Jalen Hurts and Rhyhorn both charge forward in a straight line and can't be stopped. Picture the tush push and you've pictured Rhyhorn.

clues: It owes a lot of its success to the people who stuck with it.
It spent its early days waiting its turn far down the pecking order.
Everyone looked past it, but it proved the most overlooked pick can grow into something fearsome.
A Water-type famous for being weak at first... and a {position} taken with the final pick of the draft.
Was crowned Mr. Irrelevant, now starts for the {team}, and it's a flopping orange fish that only knows Splash.
sets.why: Brock Purdy was the very last pick of the 2022 draft. Magikarp is the Pokémon everyone ignores, until it becomes something nobody can ignore.

clues: It brings a joyful energy wherever it goes.
Rivals can never quite keep track of it, no matter how closely they watch.
Playful and able to learn almost any skill, it loves to dance after showing off.
A mythical Psychic-type treasure... and an LSU {position} who won Offensive Player of the Year.
Does the Griddy for the {team}, and it's a tiny pink cat-like creature said to hold every Pokémon's DNA.
sets.why: Justin Jefferson can run every route and do anything on the field, like Mew, which can learn every move. Both are rare, graceful and playful.

clues: Once it gets loose, it leaves a blazing trail behind it.
Give it a little open space and it ignites into something nobody can catch.
It sat out a whole season, then reappeared in a dazzling flash of flame.
A Fire-type legendary bird... and a {position} who went fifth overall and won {sport} Offensive Rookie of the Year.
Reunited in the pros with its LSU quarterback, wears #{number} for the {team}, and it's the flaming legendary bird.
sets.why: Ja'Marr Chase catches a short pass and then streaks away like fire. Moltres is the legendary firebird, the flaming partner to Burrow's Articuno.

clues: It's a reliable go-to option that rarely takes a day off.
It always seems to draw every eye in the place.
Knock it down and it bounces right back, as if it can regrow whatever it lost.
A Water-type in its first form... and an Oklahoma {position} taken in the first round of the {sport} draft.
Wears #{number} for the {team}, and it's a brown starfish with a flashing red jewel at its core.
sets.why: CeeDee Lamb is the star wideout for the team with the star on its helmet. Staryu is a spinning star that slips free of anything.

clues: It plays with a scrappy, never-back-down attitude.
It doesn't mind getting physical, happily shoving bigger opponents around.
It scuttled up from the late rounds and set rookie records almost immediately.
A Water-type still in its first form... and a {position} who transferred to BYU before entering the {sport}.
Wears #{number} for the {team}, and it's a little orange crab whose giant pincers crush whatever they grip.
sets.why: Puka Nacua was a fifth-round pick with a vise grip on every catch and a love of blocking. That's Krabby: a young catcher with crushing claws.

clues: It's a rare blend of size and power that few others can match.
It's friendly and easygoing until it's time to go to work.
It looks too heavy to fly, yet it can plow straight through or leap clean over anything in its way.
A Dragon-type in its final form... and a Penn State {position} who once ran for 2,000 yards in a season.
Wears #{number} for the {team}, once hurdled a tackler backward, and it's a chubby orange dragon with tiny wings.
sets.why: Saquon Barkley has a bruiser's body but flies over defenders, just like Dragonite, the bulky, friendly dragon that can still take flight.

clues: It carries itself like it's the one in charge.
A single swipe can send an opponent tumbling to the ground.
Enormous and only stronger as the fight drags on, it rules the late stages like royalty.
A Poison/Ground final form... and a Heisman-winning {position} from Alabama with a legendary stiff-arm.
Stiff-arms tacklers for the {team}, and it's a huge purple beast with a poison horn and a pole-snapping tail.
sets.why: Derrick Henry's nickname is King Henry, and Nidoking bulldozes everything in its path. Both are huge bruisers that get stronger as the fight goes on.

clues: It can adapt into whatever its situation demands.
It's as comfortable in one role as another, which makes it hard to plan against.
Its family tree is absolutely packed with talent.
A Normal-type with many possible futures... and a Stanford {position} who's a threat as a runner and receiver.
Wears #{number} for the {team}, and it's a fluffy brown fox-like creature that can evolve many different ways.
sets.why: Christian McCaffrey does it all: run, catch, block. Eevee can become whatever the moment needs. Both come from talented families (Ed McCaffrey is his dad).

clues: Opponents always have to plan around it.
It spends most of its time chasing down whatever it's hunting.
When angry it destroys everything, and its size and speed don't seem like they should coexist.
A Water/Flying menace... and a Texas A&M {position} who went first overall and won Defensive Player of the Year.
Hunts quarterbacks for the {team}, and it's a furious blue sea serpent that evolved from a flopping fish.
sets.why: Myles Garrett is a freak of size and speed who rampages off the edge, like Gyarados, the furious sea serpent nobody can contain.

clues: It loves an audience and puffs up when the spotlight finds it.
It always seems to find the soft, open spots and settle right in.
It's at its most dangerous in the biggest moments, then celebrates louder than anyone.
A Normal-type in its final form... and a three-time champion {position} with a hit podcast alongside its brother.
Wears #{number} for the {team}, catches passes from a superstar QB, and it's a pink balloon puffball with long ears.
sets.why: Travis Kelce is a crowd-pleaser who loves the spotlight and puffs up when it finds him, just like Wigglytuff, the balloon Pokémon that evolves from Jigglypuff.

clues: It's sturdy, protective and happiest when it's shielding its companions.
It loves a good body slam and celebrates every one it lands.
Its tough, armored body delivers heavy hits, then rumbles forward with surprising speed.
A Poison/Ground final form... and a former fifth-round {position} from Iowa who blocks like a pro wrestler.
Wears #{number} for the {team}, and it's a blue, armored, spiky beast that's the matriarch of its line.
sets.why: George Kittle blocks with joyful violence and protects his teammates. Nidoqueen is sturdy and powerful, and fiercely protects its young.

clues: It looked comfortable from the very first day it showed up.
It does its best work on the ground at full speed, even though it could take to the air.
Its calm head and its quick legs seem to work independently of each other.
A two-headed Normal/Flying bird... and a Heisman-winning {position} who became Offensive Rookie of the Year.
Wears #{number} for the {team}, threw a famous rookie Hail Mary, and it's a two-headed bird that runs, not flies.
sets.why: Jayden Daniels is a true dual threat: he runs and he throws. Doduo has two heads and would rather sprint than fly.

clues: It never stops moving and seems to be everywhere at once.
It's active almost every moment and rarely needs a breather.
It's equally at home attacking and defending, swooping in from any direction.
A Poison/Flying first form... and a Heisman-winning two-way star out of Colorado.
Plays both ways for the {team}, went second overall, and it's an eyeless blue bat with purple wings.
sets.why: Travis Hunter plays receiver and cornerback and never leaves the field. Zubat is everywhere at once, flying both ways without stopping.

clues: It has a reputation for being a little different from the rest.
It's been written off as finished more than once, only to come back.
It comes from an older era, and it once sank deep before someone finally picked it up.
A Rock/Water fossil revived from ancient remains... and a four-time MVP {position} with a Super Bowl MVP too.
Wears #{number} for the {team}, and it's a blue, spiral-shelled ancient creature revived from a helix fossil.
sets.why: Aaron Rodgers is a timeless survivor with old-school wisdom. He slid on draft day and keeps coming back, like Omanyte, revived from an ancient fossil.

clues: It's at its most dangerous with just a little open space.
It doesn't need much room to make a big impact.
Small and quick, it scurries through the tiniest cracks and is gone before anyone notices.
A Normal-type in its first form... and a first-round {position} out of Alabama who catches like a receiver.
Wears #{number} for the {team}, and it's a small purple rodent with long, sharp front teeth.
sets.why: Jahmyr Gibbs hits the hole in a flash and is gone, just like Rattata, the small, lightning-quick Pokémon that darts through any crack.

clues: It isn't flashy, but the results speak for themselves.
It wins in ways that look almost too simple to work.
It looks half-asleep and never hurries, yet it's somehow always a step ahead of everyone.
A pink Water/Psychic-type, and a Serbian {position} who went from 41st pick to MVP.
Wears #{number} for the {team}, loves horse racing, and has a spiky bivalve biting its tail.
sets.why: Nikola Jokić and Slowbro both look sleepy and unbothered, then bend the game with their minds. Jokić's no-look passes are pure Psychic-type.

clues: It's smooth enough to make difficult things look routine.
It rarely panics, and it seems to save its best for the biggest moments.
Cool and graceful, it glides past rivals without breaking a sweat, leaving them stuck in place.
A legendary Ice/Flying-type, and a Canadian {position} who went one-and-done at Kentucky.
Wears #{number} for the {team}, owns the midrange, and is a blue legendary bird with a long, flowing tail.
sets.why: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and Articuno are both ice-cold and graceful: rare legends that glide past everyone. Fittingly, SGA hails from snowy Canada.

clues: It takes its craft extremely seriously.
It does things that seem to break the usual rules of what's possible.
Its arrival was hyped like nothing before, and it towers over everyone it faces.
A legendary Psychic-type built to be the strongest, and a French {position} taken first overall.
This French phenom wears #{number} for the {team}, and was cloned from a tiny pink mythical.
sets.why: Victor Wembanyama and Mewtwo are both unlike anything seen before: towering, freakishly gifted beings that seem designed in a lab to be unbeatable.

clues: It loves having the spotlight all to itself.
It does things its own way, and somehow it keeps working.
It toys with opponents like it's a game and can pick up any move it has ever seen.
A mythical Psychic-type, and a Slovenian {position} who was EuroLeague MVP as a teenager.
Wears #{number} for the {team}, is famous for its step-back, and is a tiny pink mythical with a long tail.
sets.why: Luka Dončić and Mew are both rare, playful geniuses that seem to know every move in the game, and both were legends before most people ever saw them.

clues: It stays upbeat and loose, even when things go wrong.
It doesn't need to get close to do damage.
Small and easy to underestimate, it picks off targets from far away with impossible-looking shots.
A tiny Water-type sharpshooter, and a {position} from Davidson who won the first unanimous MVP.
Wears #{number} for the {team}, changed the game from deep, and is a tiny blue seahorse that shoots jets of water.
sets.why: Stephen Curry and Horsea are both small, precise long-range shooters: Horsea snipes bugs out of the air with jets of water, and Curry snipes from deep.

clues: It's never short on confidence.
It loves the big stage and seems to feed off the noise.
Loud and brash, it soars high and then comes crashing down with thunderous force.
A No. 1 overall pick from Georgia, and a legendary Electric/Flying bird that roars out of thunderclouds.
Wears #{number} for the {team}, posterizes anyone in its way, and is a spiky yellow legendary bird.
sets.why: Anthony Edwards and Zapdos are both loud, electric and explosive, striking like thunder from high above anyone in their path.

clues: Huge and heavy, it's nearly impossible to move once it plants itself in the middle.
It took a long time to reach its final form, but it was worth the wait.
A Rock-type behemoth with surprising skill, it bullies its way to the heart of every battle.
A Ground/Rock giant with a drill on its snout, and a Cameroon-born {position} who starred at Kansas.
Wears #{number} for the {team}, missed its first two seasons, and is a gray, upright beast with a drill horn.
sets.why: Joel Embiid and Rhydon are both massive, armored and dominant near the basket, and both needed a long wait before reaching their final form.

clues: It's a fighter that never backs down from a challenge.
It carries a parent's legacy with it into every fight.
Undersized but tough, this gritty Ground-type stays low and clubs its way through crowds.
A Ground-type that swings a bone like a club, and a former second-round pick turned star {position}.
Leads the {team} in #{number} after two titles at Villanova, and wears a skull as a helmet.
sets.why: Jalen Brunson and Marowak are both undersized but gritty and battle-tested, and both carry a parent's legacy (Brunson's dad Rick played in the NBA).

clues: It's got a big personality that crowds can't get enough of.
It can go off at any moment, and when it does, the whole place feels it.
Smaller than many rivals, it stores up energy and releases it in sudden, dazzling bursts.
The most famous Electric-type of all, and a Louisville product who once scored 71 in a game.
Wears #{number} for the {team}, won the 2018 Slam Dunk Contest, and is a yellow mouse with red cheeks.
sets.why: Donovan Mitchell and Pikachu are both small, electric fan favorites that store up energy and then light up the room in a flash.

clues: Calm and calculating, it seems to see the play before it happens.
Already strong, but everyone agrees it hasn't reached its final form yet.
A Psychic-type that controls the action with its mind and sets the pace of every battle.
A Psychic-type with a star on its forehead, and a No. 1 overall pick out of Oklahoma State.
Runs the show for the {team} in #{number}, and this mustached Psychic-type always holds a bent spoon.
sets.why: Cade Cunningham and Kadabra are both already powerful minds that control the pace, and both are still on the way to their final form.

clues: It's hard to contain once it gets going.
It can strike from places rivals don't expect.
Long, thin and hard to block, it's famous for moving between teams, which is exactly how it evolves.
A purple Ghost-type with floating hands, and a four-time Olympic gold medalist {position}.
Wears #{number} for the {team}, was drafted second by Seattle, and is a grinning purple specter with no arms.
sets.why: Kevin Durant and Haunter are both long, slender and ghostly, with shots that float over everything. Haunter evolves by trade, and KD has been traded plenty.

clues: It's still young, but it already carries itself like a veteran.
Rivals find it much tougher than its frame suggests.
Long, slender and graceful with surprising reach, it's still evolving into its final form.
A rare, elegant Dragon-type that swats shots for a living in the {sport}.
Wears #{number} for the {team} after starring at Gonzaga, and its first form is a tiny serpent.
sets.why: Chet Holmgren and Dragonair are both long, slender and graceful, with surprising reach, and both are still evolving into their final form.

clues: It's mature and composed beyond what you'd expect.
It's good at a little bit of everything, and still getting better.
Young and rare, it keeps shedding its old skin as it grows bigger and stronger.
A baby Dragon-type once thought to be a myth, and a No. 1 overall pick from Maine by way of Duke.
Wears #{number} for the {team}, went first overall in 2025, and is a small blue serpent with a white forehead bulb.
sets.why: Cooper Flagg and Dratini are both rare young talents in their first stage, already special and destined to grow into superstars.

clues: It brings out the best in those who fight beside it.
It's been seen in more than one place, and it always draws a crowd.
It keeps rising long after rivals fade, and as one of a legendary trio it once brought the Heat.
A legendary Fire/Flying bird, and a No. 1 pick who came straight out of high school in Ohio.
Wears #{number} for the {team}, is the {sport}'s all-time leading scorer, and is a legendary firebird.
sets.why: LeBron James and Moltres are both legendary flames that keep rising season after season. LeBron even formed a 'Big Three' with the Miami Heat.

clues: It plays with a relentless, all-out motor.
Once it gets moving toward a target, nothing in its way seems to matter.
Raw and overlooked at first, it transformed into a long, powerful force that covers ground in a blink.
A towering Water/Flying serpent famed for its rage, and a Greek {position} with two MVPs.
Wears #{number} for the {team}, won a 2021 ring in Milwaukee, and is a huge blue serpent born from a flopping fish.
sets.why: Giannis Antetokounmpo and Gyarados both grew from skinny, overlooked beginnings into towering, unstoppable forces of nature.

clues: It's thrilling to watch when it's at its best.
It attacks from above with acrobatic dives that seem to defy gravity.
A fearless mid-stage Flying-type that swoops on bigger targets and loves aerial acrobatics.
A crested Normal/Flying bird with sharp talons, and a former No. 2 pick from Murray State.
Wears #{number} for the {team}, was drafted by Memphis, and is a brown bird with a red-and-yellow crest.
sets.why: Ja Morant and Pidgeotto both swoop in from above with fearless, high-flying attacks on targets much bigger than themselves.

clues: It's clever, patient, and always working an angle.
It has a signature move everyone knows is coming, yet few can stop.
Its unhurried back-and-forth rhythm lulls opponents into a trance before it strikes.
A fully evolved Psychic-type that eats dreams, and a former MVP and scoring champ with a famous step-back.
Wears #{number} for the {team}, won MVP in Houston, and is the evolved dream-eater that swings a pendulum.
sets.why: James Harden and Hypno are both crafty veterans that lull defenders with a steady rhythm before they strike.

clues: Always in your face, it simply will not leave you alone.
Its mouth is easily its most famous feature.
A pesky Poison-type that screeches nonstop to keep track of everything around it.
A Poison/Flying-type pest, and a second-round pick who became Defensive Player of the Year.
A four-time champ from Michigan State in #{number} for the {team}, it's a blue bat with a gaping, fanged mouth.
sets.why: Draymond Green and Golbat are both relentless pests with famously big mouths, and they never leave foes alone.

clues: It tends to show up biggest when the most is on the line.
It's patient and calculated, never wasting energy it doesn't need to spend.
It rarely makes a sound, but its one oversized feature crushes whatever it grabs.
A Water-type with a massive pincer, and a two-time Finals MVP and two-time Defensive Player of the Year.
Wears #{number} for the {team}, hit a four-bounce Game 7 buzzer-beater, and is a big red crab.
sets.why: Kawhi Leonard and Kingler both have enormous grabbers that clamp down on anything, and both pick their moments to save their heavy-duty power.

clues: It's the steady presence everyone else leans on.
It can handle opponents of just about any size.
It can wall off almost anything, and its tough exterior shields it from attackers big and small.
A spiky Water/Ice-type fortress, and a {position} from Kentucky who can switch onto anyone.
Anchors the {team} defense in #{number}, has two Olympic golds, and is a spiky bivalve with a dark face inside.
sets.why: Bam Adebayo and Cloyster are both nearly impenetrable defensive walls that can stonewall attackers of any size.

clues: It's remarkably humble for something so powerful.
It's far more versatile than most of its peers.
Experts say it can do almost anything, and many doubted such a creature could truly exist.
A mythical marvel from Japan that became the {sport}'s first 50-homer, 50-steal player.
Wears #{number} for the {team} as a two-way MVP, and it's the tiny pink mythical with every creature's DNA.
sets.why: Ohtani pitches and hits at an MVP level, like Mew, the mythical said to carry the DNA of every Pokémon and to know every move.

clues: It is enormous, calm, and built to move heavy things a very long way.
Others count on it to do the heavy lifting, and it never complains about the load.
A towering Fighting-type with arms to spare, it sends baseballs into orbit.
It once set the AL single-season homer record; its power is so vast it wears a belt to rein it in.
Wears #{number} as captain of the {team}, and it's the four-armed final form with a champion's belt.
sets.why: Judge pairs overwhelming power with quiet discipline, like Machamp, the four-armed Fighting-type whose belt holds its strength in check.

clues: It's supremely confident, and it isn't shy about showing it.
It seems to know what's coming before it arrives, and refuses anything it doesn't like.
An unnervingly calm Psychic powerhouse with an elite eye that walks and shuffles after taking pitches.
A Dominican prodigy who won a World Series in Washington while barely out of its teens.
Wears #{number} for the {team} as a lefty walk machine, and it's the lab-made legend cloned from a mythical.
sets.why: Soto reads pitches like a mind reader. Mewtwo, the lab-built Psychic legend, is the ultimate mind in the Pokémon world.

clues: It's well liked by just about everyone it works with.
Give it any role and before long it looks like it was born to play it.
It won Gold Gloves in the outfield, then reinvented itself as an infielder, a perfect copycat.
A Normal-type mimic that won an MVP and a title in Boston, and even bowls perfect games for fun.
Wears #{number} for the {team} as a do-everything champion, and it's the purple blob that only knows Transform.
sets.why: Betts went from Gold Glove right fielder to second base to shortstop. Ditto transforms into whatever it needs to be.

clues: Its energy is contagious to everyone around it.
Rivals know that if they blink, it'll already be gone.
Its explosive speed leaves everyone behind, and rivals hurry once it starts rolling.
A blazing {position} picked second overall out of a Texas high school in 2019.
Wears #{number} for the {team}, a big-league pitcher's son, and it's the evolved, upside-down ball that explodes.
sets.why: Witt is one of the fastest players in baseball, and Electrode was the fastest Pokémon of Gen 1, both liable to explode at any moment.

clues: Its raw tools make every single appearance feel like an event.
Its power is so untamed that nobody, maybe not even itself, knows what's coming next.
A towering, switch-hitting Electric-type whose throws and sprints both register off the charts.
Signed out of the Dominican Republic, it hit for the cycle as a rookie {position}.
Wears #{number} for the {team} as a base-stealing giant; it's the yellow, tiger-striped blackout maker.
sets.why: De La Cruz has wild, crackling tools that light up any game, like Electabuzz, whose stored electricity can black out a city.

clues: It's become a fan favorite with a huge following.
It grew from a modest start into a powerhouse remarkably fast.
It trained at a flight academy before finding its calling: breathing triple-digit heat.
It won a college title at LSU, went first overall, and started an All-Star Game as a rookie.
Wears #{number} for the {team} as a No. 1 pick, and it's the orange, winged starter with a flaming tail.
sets.why: Skenes (an Air Force Academy alum) throws fire and became an ace almost instantly. Charizard is the flying, fire-breathing final starter.

clues: It's a cheerful presence that's easy to root for.
Its power is the first thing anyone notices about it.
Sturdy, round and hard to move, it smashes back whatever's thrown at it like an avalanche.
Born in Montreal to a Hall of Fame father, it once launched 91 homers in a single Home Run Derby.
Wears #{number} for the {team} at {position}, and it's the rocky boulder that fully evolves only through a trade.
sets.why: Vlad Jr. is a solid, powerful slugger who hits the ball like a rockslide. Golem is a living boulder that rolls downhill.

clues: It's a team-first presence that others count on.
It does a lot of the dirty work that rarely makes headlines.
It fiercely protects those in its care, crouching low and carrying a lot of weight for the group.
A {position} from Florida State whose 2022 walk-off homer ended a two-decade playoff drought.
Wears #{number} for the {team} as a slugging backstop, and it's the kangaroo-like mom with a baby in its pouch.
sets.why: Raleigh is a tough catcher who guards his pitching staff, like Kangaskhan, the fierce parent that protects the baby in its pouch.

clues: It's got charm to spare, and fans adore it.
It comes alive under the night lights and seems to bring good luck to those around it.
Its sunny, cheerful style hides a tough, rare creature that handles the infield's most demanding spot.
Puerto Rico's pride, drafted in the first round by Cleveland, it's a Fairy with Gold Gloves.
Wears #{number} for the {team} as a grinning switch-hitter, and it's the pink moon-dancer evolved by a Moon Stone.
sets.why: Lindor is a charming, smiling leader who is tougher than he looks. Clefable is the beloved, rare Fairy that dances under the moon.

clues: It patrols a huge territory and snatches things right out of the sky.
It plays like a throwback to another era, yet its energy feels brand new.
A Rock/Flying predator that covers acres of grass and robs would-be extra-base hits.
A Dominican-born {position} who won AL Rookie of the Year in 2022.
Wears #{number} for the {team} in center field, and it's the winged fossil revived from ancient amber.
sets.why: Rodríguez covers a huge patch of center field and robs fly balls. Aerodactyl is the ancient sky predator revived from amber.

clues: It plays with a swagger that some love and some don't.
It's loyal to those who believe in it.
Majestic and impossible to ignore, its species is officially classified as legendary.
This Dominican star's father once hit two grand slams in a single inning.
Wears #{number} for the {team} as a flashy {position}, and it's the majestic orange dog evolved by a Fire Stone.
sets.why: Tatis is majestic, athletic and full of fire. Arcanine, the regal fire dog, is literally classified as the Legendary Pokémon.

clues: It's a quiet presence that does its talking with results.
It doesn't need to move much to make a huge impact.
Huge and calm, it barely moves, and opponents tiptoe around it, terrified of waking it up.
Born in Cuba and traded away by the Dodgers as a prospect, it won AL Rookie of the Year in 2019.
Wears #{number} for the {team} as a hulking Cuban lefty; it's the giant sleeper only a flute can wake.
sets.why: Alvarez is enormous, relaxed and devastating once he swings. Snorlax is the giant, sleepy Pokémon you really don't want to wake.

clues: A compact package with a startling amount of energy stored inside.
Every step crackles; it can beat you with a jolt of power or a burst of speed.
An Electric-type from Venezuela that steals bases as easily as it hits homers.
NL Rookie of the Year in 2018, then a unanimous MVP after the first 40-homer, 70-steal season.
Wears #{number} for the {team}, founded the 40-70 club, and it's the orange mouse evolved by a Thunder Stone.
sets.why: Acuña packs explosive power and speed into a compact frame, just like Raichu, the evolved electric mouse.

clues: It isn't the biggest of its kind, but it hides a dazzling number of tricks.
Opponents never know which of its many tricks is coming next.
A mystical Fire-type from Japan that places a deep arsenal of pitches with pinpoint precision.
It won three straight Sawamura Awards in Japan before crossing the Pacific to win a World Series.
Wears #{number} for the {team} as a Japanese ace; it's the golden fox with a fan of tails that lives 1,000 years.
sets.why: Yamamoto commands a deep, precise arsenal; each of Ninetales' many tails could be a different pitch. Both are mystical and precise.

clues: It's admired for how consistent it's been, year after year.
It's patient, and it rarely chases what it doesn't want.
Calm and never in a hurry, it waits patiently for just the right bite before reeling one in.
It won an NL MVP and a title in Atlanta, and represents Canada in international play.
Plays for the {team}, hit the first walk-off grand slam in World Series history, and it's the pink dozer that fishes with its tail.
sets.why: Freeman never panics and waits for his pitch, like Slowpoke, which dangles its tail in the water and waits for a bite.

clues: It's more dangerous than it looks.
It isn't always reliable, but when it delivers, everyone remembers.
Round and harmless-looking, it's often called on first, and when it goes off the blast is enormous.
A burly lefty who returned from a major knee injury to help the Cubs win the 2016 World Series.
A leadoff bomber who once led the NL in homers for Philly; it's the first-form red-and-white ball that self-destructs.
sets.why: Schwarber trades contact for colossal power, and when he connects the result is an explosion, just like Voltorb.

clues: It's admired by rivals almost as much as by its own side.
It's spent years quietly lurking near the very top of its field.
It's haunted the same neighborhood its whole career, and it's obsessed with the weather.
Drafted out of a New Jersey high school, it won three AL MVPs, though its kind usually evolves by trade.
Wears #{number} for the {team} as a three-time AL MVP, and it's the grinning purple shadow ghost.
sets.why: Trout is a complete, fully evolved superstar who haunts pitchers from every angle, much like Gengar lurking in the shadows.

clues: When it's at its peak, there's simply nothing else like it.
It took a less traditional route to the top than most.
It moves at breathtaking speed with ease, and its long, flowing mane drew as much notice as its pace.
A Fire-type thoroughbred that won back-to-back NL Cy Youngs with the Mets in 2018 and 2019.
Wears #{number} for the {team} as a long-haired former Mets ace, and it's the galloping horse with a mane of fire.
sets.why: deGrom pairs searing velocity with an elegant delivery (and once famous flowing hair), like Rapidash, the blazing horse with a fiery mane.

clues: It has a look and style all its own.
It shows up late, but it's often the one that decides the outcome.
Rare and a little odd, it never goes anywhere without its trusty weapon and strikes from odd angles.
A multi-time NL Reliever of the Year who rose to fame in Milwaukee.
Wears #{number} for the {team} as a lefty closer, and it's the wild duck that carries a leek everywhere.
sets.why: Hader is crafty and unorthodox with a funky slinging delivery, like Farfetch'd, the odd duck that fights with a leek.
